Synthetic reaction measurement and resource-model dataset

This is supplied simulated data, not a biological experiment, publication or
measurement of the anonymous input protein. It is separate from the declared
chemical equation panel. No correspondence between that panel's species and
the generic species here is asserted.

Synthetic subject S is represented by two declared independent simulated
preparations, synthetic-preparation-1 and synthetic-preparation-2. The endpoint
is product A per product B, expressed in mol per mol: 0.7 and 0.9 respectively.
The intended comparison is a conditional model predicting one product A per
product B against the named half_product_pair_model predicting 0.5. These are
model assumptions. They are not additional observations or target functions.
The supplied JSON stores the individual simulated ratios; no summary statistic,
uncertainty estimate or computed contrast is supplied.

The synthetic usable-batch model declares two resources within the same single
batch compartment and period. Resource 1 has 12 micromoles available; resource
2 has 6 micromoles available. The declared model consumes one micromole of
each resource per micromole of output and specifies 10 micromoles of output
demand. Within this toy model the declared resource list is complete, resources
do not regenerate and the declared quantities have no measurement spread.
These assumptions do not establish actual usable biological resources,
physiological capacity, steady-state flux or conditional reaction energetics.

The JSON and this protocol describe the same synthetic dataset. Reusing them
or asking another question about them does not create an independent dataset.
Unknown chemical identities, calibration and connection to the supplied protein
remain unknown. The original reaction reader determines which supported
components can be calculated from these declared operands.
